evidence.note: Shows current LLMs already possess a latent capacity for concise reasoning -- shorter correct paths exist within their own stochastic output distribution -- and that self-training (fine-tuning on the model's own best-of-N and few-shot-conditioned concise samples, FS-BoN) reliably elicits this capacity, cutting output length 30% on average across five model families on GSM8K/MATH with preserved accuracy, far outperforming zero-shot 'be concise' prompting and training on externally-sourced concise data.
evidence.title: Self-Training Elicits Concise Reasoning in Large Language Models
